issues.description: Method swiftExperienceDescription(): the problem statement (and the template) specify an instance method swiftExperienceDescription() that returns a String and instructs callers to print its returned String. The solution implementation defines swiftExperienceDescription() with return type Void and performs printing inside the method. This creates an API mismatch: students following the problem/template will implement and use a String-returning method (calling print(self.swiftExperienceDescription()) in the initializer), but the solution uses a Void-returning method that prints internally. The mismatch can confuse students about the required signature and how to consume the method's output (return vs direct print).
issues.suggestedFix: Make the solution match the problem statement and template: change the solution's extension method signature to func swiftExperienceDescription() -> String, remove any internal print calls from that method, and return the appropriate description strings. In the Developer initializer, call print(self.swiftExperienceDescription()) (as the problem instructs). This preserves the intended API (a String-returning description) and keeps printing behavior in callers (initializer and client). Alternatively, if maintainers prefer the method to print internally, update the problem statement and template to specify a Void-returning method that performs printing — but the preferred fix is to return String in the solution.
